run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: I checked the hotel-reservation application across Kubernetes state, events, Jaeger traces, Prometheus span and application metrics, and Loki logs inside the authorized window (2026-11-23T08:49:12Z to 2026-11-24T08:49:12Z). The application was deployed only at 2026-11-24T08:47:25Z, so observable application runtime is roughly 1m47s (08:47:25-08:49:12). Within that period I found no service-side failure: all 21 pods were Running with 0 restarts, every hotel-reservation Deployment had 1 ready replica, every hotel-reservation Service endpoint had 0 not-ready addresses, all eight per-service blackbox probes returned 1, the only status_code value on traces_span_metrics_calls_total is STATUS_CODE_UNSET (no error-status series exists), service p95 span latency at 08:49:12 was at most 4.52 ms (frontend), the frontend HTTP GET /hotels bucket set contains no span above the 25 ms bucket, and the rate and search self-instruments reported 0 expired, 0 rejected, 0 failed and 0 timed-out requests. The request-rate and connection anomalies I could trace to an object are (a) a wrk2 load generator pod (wrk2-job-hmmpk) driving the frontend Service IP 10.96.151.68:5000 at about 98 req/s with 3 threads and 100 connections, which matches the HighRequestRate alerts observed later for frontend/search/profile/rate/reservation, and (b) the same generator's own logs reporting 195 and 189 socket timeouts per 30-second round, for which no server-side slowdown is visible. Separately, and with no evidence tying them to the reservation services, the audit-log-archiver CronJob pods in the same namespace never report Ready (the archiver container ends with exit code 0, Completed, while the fluent-bit sidecar keeps running) and that sidecar is CPU-throttled against a 50m limit. Because I could not establish a service-side fault, or a change that caused one, I report a partial assessment with candidates and explicit gaps rather than a confirmed root cause.

The traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds counters show mongo_rate as 62 spans with a cumulative mean of 1.561 ms and mongo_profile as 61 spans with a mean of 1.043 ms, i.e. the rate and profile services' MongoDB client spans completed with normal per-query durations.

A trace of frontend HTTP GET /hotels at 08:49:11Z completed in 4.304 ms with http.status_code 200 and a consistent child tree (frontend /search.Search/Nearby 2.041 ms -> search 1.438 ms -> geo 0.026 ms and rate 0.375 ms; frontend /reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability 1.020 ms; frontend /profile.Profile/GetProfiles 0.700 ms), with no error status on any span.

The error-matching Loki query over namespace hotel-reservation between 08:47:30Z and 08:49:12Z returned frontend "grpc/lb/consul: error retrieving instances from Consul ... connection refused" lines stamped 08:47:26Z (frontend startup, before the query start), MongoDB "NamespaceNotFound: config.system.sessions does not exist" session-reap lines from the mongo pods, and the two wrk2 "Socket errors ... timeout" summary lines; it returned no error line from the frontend/search/rate/geo/profile/reservation/recommendation/user request handlers.

The HighRequestRate alert on frontend, search, profile, rate and reservation is load-driven rather than a service fault: pod wrk2-job-hmmpk generated about 98 req/s with 100 connections against the frontend Service, and at 08:49:12 the same services showed no error status, p95 span latency at most 4.52 ms, and zero rejected/expired/failed requests in their own counters.

The 195 and 189 wrk2 socket timeouts per 30-second round are client- or connection-level rather than slow application responses: the traces returned all show http.status_code 200, the frontend HTTP GET /hotels pool contains no span above the 25 ms bucket, and the generator's own max latency was about 10 ms, so no server-side mechanism for those timeouts is visible in the supplied evidence.

The audit-log-archiver not-ready condition follows from that CronJob's own pod template: a short-lived archiver container that ends with exit code 0 (Completed) alongside a long-running nc-based fluent-bit-sidecar, so the pod never reports Ready, and the sidecar runs under a 50m CPU limit that is being throttled; no evidence links those pods to the hotel-reservation service graph.

A latency fault in a hotel-reservation service is not supported: at 08:49:12 every service p95 was at or below 4.52 ms and the frontend HTTP GET /hotels bucket set contains no span above the 25 ms bucket.

A MongoDB admin-privilege revocation fault on the rate or geo database (the namespace does contain ConfigMaps failure-admin-rate and failure-admin-geo with scripts that revoke the admin user's readWrite role) is not supported by the observed signals: rate's 62 mongo_rate client spans averaged 1.561 ms, search_rate_failures_total and search_rate_timeouts_total were 0 with 5062 attempts and 5062 successes, and mongodb-rate/mongodb-geo logged successful admin authentication from the rate and geo pod addresses.

Pod-level failure of the reservation services (CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled, Evicted, Pending, Unschedulable) is not supported: all 21 pods were Running with 0 restarts, all 19 deployments reported 1 ready replica, and every hotel-reservation Service endpoint had 0 not-ready addresses.

Nothing in the observed data shows customer-visible failure of the hotel-reservation services: all eight service blackbox probes returned 1, all Services had ready endpoints, span status stayed Unset with no error series, p95 latency stayed in the low milliseconds, and the rate/search self-instruments reported zero failures, zero timeouts, zero rejections and zero expirations.

gaps: No metric history is available for the window: range queries such as sum(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend"}) over 2026-11-24T08:20:00Z-08:49:12Z and over the full window returned no series (status no_data), and instant queries returned a single sample at 08:49:12, so no pre-incident baseline or change time can be established.

The query for a p99 latency threshold (histogram_quantile(0.99, ...) > 50) returned no data (status no_data); absence of a p99 above 50 ms is therefore unchecked, and only the p95 quantiles and the frontend HTTP GET /hotels bucket bounds are established.
The audit-log-archiver pod inventory query returned 5 pods and the job list 3 jobs at the query instants; earlier or later state in the window is unknown, and the CronJob's churn is only sampled.

The hotel-reservation application existed for only about 1m47s inside the 24-hour window (deployment creation timestamps 2026-11-24T08:47:25Z, earliest pod activity 08:47:26Z); state before that and after 08:49:12 is unknown, and alerts observed at 08:50:26Z and later fall outside the authorized window.

The wrk2 load generator's Job/pod definition, script and socket-timeout setting could not be read (pod wrk2-job-hmmpk is no longer present in the cluster and direct pod-log read was refused), so only its Loki log lines are available and the mechanism behind 195/189 socket timeouts per round is unconfirmed.

No HTTP response payload is observable in traces or logs, so whether /hotels, /reservation and /user return correct (non-empty) results is unverified; a functional regression that keeps HTTP 200 and low latency would not appear in the evidence I have.

MongoDB credentials and roles cannot be read (secrets are not readable), and no change-history source is integrated, so whether a role revocation or other post-deployment configuration change was applied outside the sampled instants could not be verified.

The failing blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe targets ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx, but the deployment query for namespace ingress-nginx returned no matches (status no_data) and no Ingress objects exist; whether an ingress path is expected for this app, or why that probe fails, is unknown.

Span-derived data is incomplete: Jaeger returned no traces for operation HTTP POST /reservation or HTTP POST /user in the window, and the span counters (1930 HTTP GET /hotels spans) are far below the wrk2 request counts (5905 in two rounds), so span counts cannot be read as request counts and the untraced portion is unknown.

Whether the audit-log-archiver CronJob (its sidecar design and 50m CPU limit) is intended in this environment or incidental noise is unknown; no evidence ties it to the hotel-reservation service graph.
next_steps: Retrieve the wrk2 Job/pod spec and its script/timeout arguments from the workload manifest or harness to explain the roughly 6% client socket timeouts.
Compare the observed 08:47-08:49 window against a baseline deployment of the same app (the alert rules reference a blueprint-hotel-reservation namespace) before treating ~100 req/s as abnormal.

Exercise the frontend API and inspect response bodies to confirm hotel, rate and profile data are correct; if results are empty, check authorization on geo-db and rate-db (for example db.currentUser roles) given the failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate ConfigMaps present in the namespace.
Decide whether an ingress path is required for hotel-reservation; if so, deploy an ingress controller and the Ingress resource that the blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe targets.
Review the audit-log-archiver CronJob pod template (short-lived archiver plus long-running nc sidecar, 50m CPU limit) if those not-ready and throttling alerts are meant to be actionable.
Enable longer metric retention or scrape history so rate and latency deviations can be attributed to a time rather than to a single snapshot.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

{"remove-admin-mongo.sh":"#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

echo "Removing admin user..."

mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.dropUser('admin');"

echo "Admin user removed successfully"
","remove-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh":"#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Recreating admin user..."

# Connect to MongoDB and create the admin user
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

echo "Admin user recreated"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges restored successfully"
","revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh":"#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
# TARGET_DB="rate-db"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Downgrading admin user privileges..."

# Connect to MongoDB and revoke roles
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.revokeRolesFromUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: 'readWrite', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges downgraded"

echo "Privilege restored successfully"
"}

{"k8s-geo-mongo.sh":"#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"

ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

TARGET_DB="geo-db"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"

echo "Waiting for MongoDB to start..."
until mongo --eval "print('waited for connection')" > /dev/null 2>&1; do
  sleep 1
done
echo "MongoDB started"

# Create the admin user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating admin user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

# Create the root user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating root user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ROOT_USER', pwd: '$ROOT_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database to root
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ROOT_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ROOT_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"


echo "Initialization script completed"
"}
